notes.text: Raw Kev answers directly choose commit_default in all72 cases; controller did not substitute a fallback or suppress tool actions.

All decisions expose21 actions, including9 Chronos configuration requests,4 analog strategies,3 inspection tools,search,review,and3 actions returning the same default. No deadline,byte,API or candidate exhaustion is present.

Initial state contains numerical flags and the default prediction summary, but no retrieved analog evidence or actual competing prediction. Initial mature_feedback is empty because initial_observation calls summarize_state(context) without the feedback argument; inspect_state/inspect_feedback remain available.
Real external evidence is unavailable in this run; search_evidence remains offered. Twenty-five origins have nontrivial registered numerical state flags and still directly commit default.

Flat joint action choice mixes information gathering and immediate termination. Nine forecast options and multiple retrieval options split choice mass while default submission is immediately executable; staged planning/submission could yield different tool usage. These probabilities do not establish a causal explanation or forecast confidence.

Three semantically overlapping default-return actions and concatenating all seven skills, including abstention/review language, may encourage premature stopping. Test semantic grouping, deduplicated choices and phase-specific skill prompts in a separate release; action permutation checks can diagnose ordering sensitivity.

An optional minimum evidence acquisition protocol before submission can validate runtime module coverage without forcing a preferred forecast or making an accuracy claim. Alternatively show mature-feedback/analog-availability summaries in initial state to let the planner judge tool value.

Read-only audit of completed run. No source,skill,model,request or prediction changed; no extra API calls; no accuracy-based optimization. This is engineering coverage evidence, not proof of predictive benefit.
